title: Partner who shot teen 'saved my life,' officer says
article: The way Toronto police officer Allan Love sees it, he's alive today because his partner killed Jeffrey Reodica two years ago.

The policeman told a coroner's inquest yesterday how, on May 21, 2004, he and Detective Constable Dan Belanger were on the ground struggling to handcuff the 17-year-old when his partner shouted, "Knife! Knife!"

Det. Constable Love said he recoiled and, a split second later, a blade whipped past his face. Three shots blazed, he said, and Mr. Reodica fell onto his stomach with a black-handled knife still clutched in his left hand. The teen died in hospital three days later.
"Officer Belanger saved my life," said Det. Constable Love, 32.

That May afternoon, shortly after 4, the two plainclothes officers had rushed to a residential neighbourhood in Scarborough after a slew of 911 calls reported a group of armed teens chasing three other youths.

The pair were part of a plainclothes major-crime unit, but the two experienced officers, dressed in jeans and casual shirts, raced to the scene in their black Chevy Malibu because no marked units were available, Det. Constable Love said.
One of the central questions at the inquest, which began May 8, is whether Mr. Reodica or his friends knew that the men were police officers.

While some witnesses said they knew the men were police, others, including some of Mr. Reodica's mostly Filipino friends, said they thought the men were related to the white teens they had been pursuing because of an alleged racist incident in a schoolyard the day before.

Barry Swadron, the lawyer for the Reodica family, pressed the officer on whether he and his partner could have done more to calm the situation. Mr. Reodica's family maintains that the teen wouldn't have resisted if he knew the men were officers.
Det. Constable Love said he told one of Mr. Reodica's friends that he was a police officer. Meanwhile, his partner was speaking with Mr. Reodica about three metres away.
The situation quickly escalated when the teen refused to get on the ground, and the officer tackled him to the grass.
Det. Constable Love said he went to help and a struggle ensued. Mr. Reodica, he said, twisted from the grip of both officers, who each weighed more than 200 pounds.
Mr. Reodica was shot three times in the back.

Outside the court, Kiké Roach, lawyer for the Community Alliance for Social Justice, said the officer's testimony "didn't make sense." How could the teen wriggle away from the grip of two large men? she asked.
Det. Constable Belanger is also expected to testify this week.
